clue.text: By chance, one new score's interrupted by detectives

indicators.note: a phrase that has something break into it, so the detectives' letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
a score is a tally, the running count in a game

explanation.surface: A sports result is disrupted when police detectives barge in unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like a match result but is a running count. 'interrupted by' breaks the first word open after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs describing something happening without design or intention, by sheer luck.

clue.text: Top man, in the main

parts.note: the main is the open sea, so the top man there is the highest-ranking naval officer

explanation.surface: Someone who is, generally speaking, the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly', but 'the main' is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest rank of officer in a navy, commanding a fleet at sea.

clue.text: Gripes about Opposition's leader left in charge

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Opposition

explanation.surface: Complaints about the head of the Opposition being left to run things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripes' looks like complaints, but here it means stomach pains, as in 'the gripes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, and gripes is an old word for those spasms of the bowel.

clue.text: Bent detective was brilliant on street

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the street, so they come before it

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
shone means was brilliant, gave out bright light

explanation.surface: A corrupt detective who once excelled on the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for corrupt or crooked, someone not honest in their dealings.

clue.text: After knockout about to rise in corner

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the combined pieces are turned around
the word for about is placed after the knockout letters

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A boxer, once knocked out, gets up again in his corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or sheltered corner of a room.

clue.text: Roughly caned over extremities in true story

indicators.note: roughly suggests something done crudely, so the letters of caned are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its first and last letters, here of true

explanation.surface: Someone was beaten hard, and that's no tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' makes ANECD from CANED; 'extremities in' gives TE from true.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short account of an incident, a brief tale told in conversation.

clue.text: Shed light on that man being flexible

parts.note: lit means shed light on, illuminated
he refers to that man

explanation.surface: Illuminating a man who is proving supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and bending easily, so it is a synonym of flexible.

clue.text: With hour inside gives in, going off rails

indicators.note: the hour's letter goes inside the rearranged letters
going off the rails suggests going astray, so the letters of gives in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders and goes astray, as the clock ticks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' makes INVEIGS from GIVES IN; 'inside' puts H within it. 'rails' looks like part of 'off the rails' but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest bitterly, and to inveigh is to speak out angrily against something.

clue.text: Go off Church reading, perhaps upsetting minister

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the pieces upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to go off, decay
CE is the Church of England
reading is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it

explanation.surface: A minister so upset by a church reading that he wants to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a member of the clergy in charge of a parish, a kind of minister.

clue.text: Marker is only beyond motorway, in case

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written here as MI
lest is an old-fashioned word meaning in case
one can mean only, as in 'my one chance'

explanation.surface: A sign beside the motorway that's there just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it as the letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A milestone is a stone by a road marking the distance in miles to a place.

clue.text: Worried in the past, for instance

definitions.meaning: the past is an example of a grammatical time form of a verb

explanation.surface: Someone was anxious back then.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is nervous and strained; the other is the grammar term, of which past, present and future are examples.

clue.text: Judge concerned with jailbird pocketing grand

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: pocketing means putting into one's pocket, so the jailbird holds the grand

parts.note: a con is a convict
K is slang for a thousand pounds, a grand

explanation.surface: A judge involved with a convict who is taking a thousand pounds in bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to estimate or form an opinion, which is to judge a matter.

clue.text: The woman's wearing a hollow 'supporter'

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so the woman is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a dent is a hollow in a surface
her refers to the woman, with 's read as is

explanation.surface: A woman is dressed in what seems an empty, hollow 'supporter', perhaps a bra.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'supporter' hint at an undergarment, but the word simply means a follower.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a cause, party or person.

clue.text: Sins of large sections of Church

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
apses are the semicircular recesses at the end of a church

explanation.surface: The sins found in big parts of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapses are moral slips or failings, minor wrongdoings akin to sins.

clue.text: Coppers on alert suppressing offensive

indicators.note: to suppress is to keep something held down inside, so the answer is concealed within these words

explanation.surface: Police on standby are cracking down on an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a noun, a military attack, but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal remarks are rude ones aimed at someone's character, which makes them offensive.

clue.text: Alien phoned back endlessly outside

indicators.note: the shortened back word goes outside the word for phoned
without its end, so the last letter of the word for back is dropped

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
rang means phoned

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial phoned home, ET style, and kept going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is a ship's rear, not 'returning'; 'endlessly' trims its last letter, and 'outside' wraps what remains round the word for phoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is an outsider or foreigner, someone unfamiliar, the older sense of alien.

clue.text: A northern course circling radius for polar region

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the course's letters surround the radius

parts.note: a tactic is a course of action
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: Taking a northern route around a circle to reach the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points north, but the polar region is the far south.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the region around the South Pole, one of Earth's two polar regions.

clue.text: Caught in homicide, ran sneakily up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the concealed letters read from the bottom upwards
in signals that the answer sits within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A murderer sneaked away and was caught in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to DERANSNE inside 'homicide, ran sneakily'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnared means trapped as if in a snare, which is to be caught.

clue.text: Son runs into copper, facing minute analysis

indicators.note: into means the runs' letter goes inside the copper's symbol

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means tiny

explanation.surface: A boy dashes into a policeman, who examines it in tiny detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like a unit of time but is the adjective meaning very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close, critical examination, so it is a kind of detailed analysis.

clue.text: Prostrate having done in backbone …

indicators.note: in means the letter for done goes inside the word for backbone

parts.note: the spine is the backbone
U stands for upper class and so socially acceptable, the done thing, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Someone lying flat after doing their back in.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U is a British label for upper-class versus other usage, so U is 'the done thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on one's back, and prostrate means lying stretched out flat.

clue.text: Equilibrium unaltered on edges of seat

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, here of seat

parts.note: as is means left unchanged, unaltered

explanation.surface: Keeping one's balance, perched unmoved on the very edge of a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of inactivity where opposing forces balance, a kind of equilibrium.

clue.text: … rise being supported by doctor

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise
something resting on another is supported by it

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a patient's improvement is backed by medical help.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, so a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Suggest right piece of work's put inside pen

indicators.note: put inside means the two pieces are placed within the pen word

parts.note: a pound is a pen or enclosure for animals
op is short for opus, a piece of work, with 's read as is

explanation.surface: Recommending that the right piece of writing be placed in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to put forward an idea for consideration, which is to suggest it.

clue.text: More trouble going topless

indicators.note: losing its top, so the first letter of the word for trouble is removed

parts.note: bother means trouble

explanation.surface: Going topless only causes more trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional, as in 'some other examples', so it stands for more.

clue.text: Comparatively dirty canine initially more ill-bred

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of canine

parts.note: ruder means more ill-mannered, more ill-bred

explanation.surface: A dog that's a bit grubbier and less well mannered than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude can mean vulgar or smutty, so the comparative form means dirtier in that sense.

clue.text: Emirate is style capital

parts.note: to dub is to style or name someone
A1 means first-rate, capital, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A Gulf state that is a fashionable capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means excellent, A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven emirates making up the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Stone's old before tour's over

indicators.note: in a down clue before means above, so the old letter comes first
over means turned over, so the letters of lap are read backwards

parts.note: a lap is a tour of a track, with 's read as is

explanation.surface: A stone belonging to someone old, before the tour ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a semi-precious gemstone with shifting colours.

clue.text: Old under orderly facing hospital

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so the orderly word comes before the hospital

parts.note: neat means orderly, tidy
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An elderly hospital orderly working beneath a senior colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital porter, but is the adjective meaning tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic, old-fashioned shortening of beneath, meaning below.

clue.text: Queen's revolving set fitted upright

indicators.note: revolving means turning round, so the Queen's letters read backwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, with 's read as is
to put something is to set it down
able means fitted for, capable of

explanation.surface: The Queen's merry-go-round was installed standing straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputable means respectable and of good standing, like an upright, honest person.

clue.text: Bent police tried changing end of confession

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of police tried are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter, here of confession

explanation.surface: Corrupt officers altered the last part of a suspect's confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' suggests corrupt police, but here it is the noun meaning an inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination or liking, which is what a predilection is.
